name: Ameriprint Apparel
old_description: Custom Screen Printing for Schools, Teams & Corporate Apparel
about:
Ameriprint Apparel is a custom screen-printing and embroidery company based in Sun Prairie, Wisconsin. Founded in 1985, the business has served the local community and broader Wisconsin area for nearly four decades.

The company provides a range of decoration and customization services including screen printing, embroidery, direct-to-film (DTF) and digital printing, and laser engraving. It also sources and brands promotional products such as drinkware, headwear, tote bags, and office items. All production is handled in-house at its Sun Prairie facility, which includes a graphics team and an online design tool for customers.

Ameriprint serves schools, sports teams, corporate businesses, and organizations needing branded merchandise. Its customer base includes educational institutions ordering team and spirit wear, companies seeking employee appreciation kits and trade show giveaways, and groups such as the American Legion and university fraternities. The shop also handles holiday corporate gifts and promotional items for events.

The company distinguishes itself with an in-house graphics team and an online design tool that lets customers create artwork, along with inventory storage and fulfillment services for recurring orders.

name: Amphenol DC Electronics
old_description: 70,000 sq ft facility making custom cable/wire harness assemblies (Amphenol division)
about:
Amphenol DC Electronics operates from a 70,000-square-foot facility in San Jose, California, with additional manufacturing sites in Nogales, Mexico, and Malaysia. The company was founded in 1979 by David Cianciulli after he left Hughes Aircraft to start a cable sales and distribution business. Within a few years, the operation added engineers and assemblers to produce custom cable and wire harness solutions for technical instrument manufacturers. In 2013, the business was acquired by Amphenol Corporation, becoming a division known as Amphenol DC Electronics (ADCE).

ADCE specializes in the design, engineering, and manufacture of custom wire harnesses, cable assemblies, and integrated electronic mechanical devices (box builds). The company handles both high- and low-volume production runs, offering build-to-print services, prototyping, and custom tooling design.

The company serves aerospace and military customers (notably supplying Trimble with GPS cables during the first Gulf War), medical device manufacturers (MRI, patient monitoring, surgical robotics), industrial equipment makers (factory automation robots), precision agriculture (GPS and surveying equipment), and RF coaxial applications. Its client base includes defense contractors, medical OEMs, and industrial automation firms.

ADCE emphasizes its single-focus expertise in custom cable and wire harness assemblies, which the company says enables engineers to identify design flaws before production. It highlights lean manufacturing practices applied across information and material flows, in-house engineering liaison services, and a culture of continuous improvement as key differentiators.

name: Amphenol TPC Wire & Cable
old_description: Can’t seem to find a standard solution for your connector or cable needs?
about:
Amphenol TPC Wire & Cable is headquartered in Macedonia, Ohio. The company traces its roots to 1979 when it began supplying ruggedized wire and cable for harsh industrial environments.

The company manufactures high-performance wire, cable, connectors, and assemblies, along with cable management systems, cordsets, and electrical components. A dedicated engineering team of electrical, industrial, and mechanical engineers develops custom-engineered solutions tailored to specific application challenges, from severe abrasion and chemical exposure to extreme temperatures and continuous flexing.

Amphenol TPC serves a broad range of industries including automotive, food and beverage, general manufacturing, industrial automation, metals, mining, oil and gas, rail and transit, shipyard and marine, utility and power transmission, and wood, pulp, and paper. Customers such as a boilermaker leadman at a welding operation, a maintenance manager at a freezer facility, and a prep plant supervisor at a coal mine have reported reduced downtime, lower costs, and improved safety after switching to the company’s Super-Trex® and Chem-Gard® cable lines.

The company differentiates itself by focusing on abuse-resistant designs that outlast commodity cable, emphasizing a problem-solving approach that combines curiosity with qualified engineering expertise.

name: Ampleon USA Inc.
old_description: The advent of 5G NR (New Radio) since 2019 has ushered in a new era with demanding prerequisites for RF power components. Ampleon stands at the forefront, providing market leading RF power solutions for mMIMO (Massive Multiple Input Multiple Output) of up to 128 simultaneous transmit and receive streams, high efficiency small cell, and high-power macro base stations.
about:
Ampleon USA Inc. maintains its U.S. office in Smithfield, Rhode Island, as part of a global semiconductor company headquartered in Nijmegen, Netherlands. The firm operates a production site in Cabuyao, Philippines, and supports customers across the Americas through a network of sales representatives covering every U.S. state.

The company designs and manufactures RF power transistors, including gallium‑nitride‑on‑silicon‑carbide (GaN on SiC) HEMTs and silicon LDMOS devices, for 5G massive MIMO base stations, small‑cell and macro‑cell infrastructure, particle accelerators, and industrial heating systems. Its product line spans discrete transistors and integrated modules rated from kilowatts to megawatts.

Ampleon serves the telecommunications, industrial‑scientific‑medical, and research sectors. Customers include 5G network equipment makers, particle‑accelerator laboratories, and manufacturers of RF heating equipment. The ITAR registration allows the company to support defense‑related programs in the United States.

Ampleon emphasizes its solid‑state RF technology as a replacement for legacy vacuum‑tube systems, offering higher efficiency, smaller form factors, and scalable power from kilowatts to megawatts. The firm highlights its GaN on SiC HEMTs for long‑pulse applications and LDMOS transistors for high‑power discrete needs as key differentiators.

name: Amsted Automotive
old_description: Amsted Automotive Honored with Manufacturer of the Year – Large Tier & Manufacturing Export Product of the Year -
about:
Amsted Automotive is headquartered in Saginaw, Michigan. The company traces its roots to 1903 with the founding of Burgess-Norton. The current entity was formed in 2021 through the integration of Burgess-Norton (established 1903) and Means Industries (established 1922), along with Transform Automotive (1997) and SMW Manufacturing (2004). No ownership tags are disclosed.

Amsted Automotive designs and manufactures high-performance components for vehicle and industrial applications. Its product portfolio includes brackets and welded assemblies, residential and industrial coupler components, piston pins and bearing products, forestry, trenching and wear parts, and powertrain components. The company employs over 2,000 people worldwide and operates 21 manufacturing facilities across North America, Europe, and Asia, including 13 in the United States. Annual production exceeds 200 million components. Core manufacturing processes encompass advanced metal forming (flow forming, in-die spline forming, grob forming, laser welding, stamping), cold forming and finishing, powder metallurgy, and propulsion systems such as torque management and clutch technologies.

The company serves global automotive, off-highway, mining, and industrial markets. Its components are used in internal combustion, hybrid, and electric powertrains for passenger cars, heavy-duty trucks, and off-highway equipment. Customers include automakers and industrial OEMs seeking net-shape metal components and complex assemblies.

Amsted Automotive emphasizes its global footprint as a differentiator, stating that its 13 U.S.-based facilities minimize tariff risks and supply delays by enabling regional manufacturing. The company also highlights its century-long manufacturing legacy and integrated capabilities spanning metal forming, powder metallurgy, and propulsion solutions as key to delivering high-quality, cost-effective components.

name: Andersen Industries, Inc.
old_description: Large custom walk-in sheet-metal enclosures and control houses
about:
Andersen Industries, Inc. operates from a 108,000-square-foot purpose-built facility in Adelanto, California. The company was founded in 1966 as a small backyard welding repair shop and has grown into a single-source supplier for large OEMs and manufacturers.

The company provides end-to-end contract manufacturing services including engineering, sheet metal and plate fabrication, CNC machining, welding, finishing, and assembly. Its fabrication capabilities encompass CNC laser cutting, turret punching, plasma cutting, sawing, press brake forming, plate rolling, milling, and turning. In addition to contract work, Andersen designs and manufactures its own WeldPro 360 line of MIG welding booms, fume extractors, and mounting accessories. The facility features overhead cranes and ample floor space for heavy fabrication.

Andersen serves manufacturers and OEMs across retail merchandising, food services, commercial and industrial vehicles, and oil and gas. Its customer base includes specialty equipment manufacturers, machine tool builders, and contractors. Typical OEM products range from brackets, cabinets, and enclosures to generator enclosures, compressor enclosures, command centers, control centers, and structural platforms.

The company emphasizes its in-house capacity to take projects from 3D CAD design through finished product, leveraging five decades of experience and a purpose-built facility to deliver on time and to specification. Its proprietary welding equipment is built to minimize non-arc time and maximize operator productivity.

name: Andersen Manufacturing Inc
old_description: Explore a variety of our premium hitches. From 5th wheel hitches to bumper pull hitches, we have got all you need right here.
about:
Andersen Manufacturing Inc., doing business as Andersen Hitches, is headquartered in Idaho Falls, Idaho. The company was founded in 1948 and remains family-owned, having grown from a single-room shop into a 102,000-square-foot manufacturing and fabrication complex. In 2021, the facility expanded by an additional 70,000 square feet to meet rising demand.

The company designs and manufactures a full line of trailer hitches and towing accessories, including fifth-wheel connections, bumper-pull hitches, weight-distribution systems, ball mounts, trailer jacks, leveling blocks, and locking pins. Products are built from aluminum, steel, and plastic components, with many items carrying a lifetime warranty.

Andersen serves the towing industry, targeting recreational travelers, commercial haulers, and outdoor sportsmen. Its products are sold through a nationwide network of authorized dealers, and the company emphasizes support for local U.S. businesses and jobs.

The company differentiates itself through original, patent-pending designs—such as the lightweight Ultimate 5th Wheel Connection and the one-handed Rapid Pin—and by providing direct technical support from towing experts for product selection and installation. All manufacturing occurs in Idaho Falls, reinforcing its American-made positioning.

name: Anderson Electric Co.
old_description: We value a long lasting relationship with each and every client.
about:
Anderson Electric Co. is a family-owned electrical contracting firm based in Aberdeen, South Dakota. Founded in 2020 by Shaine Anderson, the company emerged after Anderson accumulated over a decade of experience in residential, commercial, and industrial electrical work, including a stint overseeing maintenance departments at a local beef processing plant. Anderson's vision centered on building healthy customer relationships and strong workplace leadership, values he codified as integrity, quality, and service.

The company designs, installs, repairs, and maintains electrical systems across residential, commercial, farm, and industrial sectors. Its service portfolio includes industrial electrical maintenance, project design, controls and automation, custom lighting, and smart home technology integration. All installed equipment carries UL listing, and the firm adheres to National Electrical Code and local fire safety standards, often exceeding minimum requirements. Anderson Electric is licensed, insured, and bonded in South Dakota, with reciprocity in other states.

Customers range from homeowners seeking wiring upgrades or smart home installations to commercial operators needing industrial maintenance and automation. Notable projects include the transformation of a 1950s church into a café, involving full electrical modernization and kitchen outlet design, as well as residential service work such as bathroom fan ducting and outlet relocation. The firm also serves agricultural and industrial clients with equipment troubleshooting and 480V switchgear expertise.

Anderson Electric distinguishes itself through a commitment to "going the extra mile," emphasizing personal consultation, employee development, and community giving. A portion of monthly revenue supports organizations such as Destiny Rescue, Coffee with a Cause, and Aberdeen's Safe Harbor. The company's focus on vetting employees for safety and investing in leadership training reflects its founding principle that a healthy workforce yields better service.

name: Andon Electronics Corporation
old_description: Andon Electronics Corporation - Innovative Socket Designs For Optimum Device Protection
about:
Andon Electronics Corporation is based in Lincoln, Rhode Island. The company is led by president John O. Tate, who developed the precision semiconductor socket contact that underpins its product line. While the founding year is not publicly disclosed, the business has established itself as a specialist in socket solutions for electronic device placement.

The company manufactures innovative precision sockets used to mount image sensors, optoelectronic sensors, gas sensors, DC‑DC converters, batteries, crystal oscillators, fuses, relays, and other electronic devices onto printed circuit boards. Its catalog spans dozens of package types — including PGA, BGA, LCC, DIP, SIP, TO, PLCC, and LED — as well as specialty items such as heat‑sink sockets, high‑temperature sockets, ultra‑low‑profile sockets, floating‑pin sockets, and laminate wafer sockets. Andon offers both standard and custom socket designs.

Andon’s sockets are used by original equipment manufacturers and contract manufacturers in industries such as camera production, laser manufacturing, gas‑sensing equipment, and broader electronic product assembly. Named customers include Chungwa Telecom Labs and Micropac Industries, indicating a presence in telecommunications and specialized industrial electronics.

The company states that its socket designs help customers avoid device damage during assembly, reduce board‑assembly labor, and improve turnaround time. This focus on device protection and assembly efficiency is presented as the core reason for its product development.
